newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet session.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded higher on Thursday for the second straight session, but yield spreads remained largely unchanged.
"We've seen relatively light activity today," said one head trader at large U.S. investment bank. He described pass-through activity as "light two-way flow."
Traders said no major bid lists were spotted.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent issues were up 3/32 at 99-03/32, yielding 94 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 4/32 at 99-04/32, and Freddie Mac issues were up 3/32 at 99-08/32.
The five-year note was up 6/32 at 6.60 percent, while the 10-year note was up 11/32 to yield 6.75 percent.

Market participants will get a handful of economic data on Friday. Most players will focus on the second estimate of first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which is slated for release at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
Economists in a Reuters poll projected a 6.0-percent annual growth rate for the period, up from the previous estimate of 5.6 percent.
